audits.title: P-109 A RETROSPECTIVE AUDIT OF THE DEPARTMENTAL USE OF PROPHYLACTIC ANTIBIOTICS IN ELECTIVE VENTRAL HERNIA SURGERY AS COMPARED TO NATIONAL AND INTERNATIONAL GUIDELINES
audits.standard: NICE, British Hernia Society and European Hernia Society guidance on prophylactic antibiotics in elective hernia repair

cycle1.result: 35/44 (79.5%) mesh repairs received prophylactic antibiotics; all laparoscopic repairs received them; 3 of 5 low-risk non-mesh open repairs received antibiotics.

audits.other_findings: Clear local guidelines and documenting reasons for giving antibiotics were recommended.
audits.citation: Islam R, Sriskanthanathan A, Maynard O, Abdalla S. P-109 A RETROSPECTIVE AUDIT OF THE DEPARTMENTAL USE OF PROPHYLACTIC ANTIBIOTICS IN ELECTIVE VENTRAL HERNIA SURGERY AS COMPARED TO NATIONAL AND INTERNATIONAL GUIDELINES. British Journal of Surgery. 2022;109(Supplement_7). doi:10.1093/bjs/znac308.207.

audits.title: WP1.9 - An audit of prophylactic antibiotic use in elective inguinal hernia repair
audits.standard: National guidance: no antibiotic prophylaxis for low-risk patients; single dose for high-risk patients
audits.setting: District general hospital, elective inguinal hernia repair (University Hospital North Durham)

cycle1.result: 53.33% of patients received antibiotics in line with national guidelines; 50.00% had prophylactic antibiotics overall

audits.other_findings: Wound infection rate 1.04% (0% with antibiotics vs 2.08% without, P = 0.175); 94.79% of repairs were open.
audits.citation: Hume C, Dunlop H. WP1.9 - An audit of prophylactic antibiotic use in elective inguinal hernia repair. British Journal of Surgery. 2024;111(Supplement_8). doi:10.1093/bjs/znae197.119.

audits.title: 727 Implementing High-Risk Criteria to Optimise Perioperative Antibiotic Use in Hernia Surgery: A Two-Cycle Audit
audits.standard: European Hernia Society guidelines: perioperative antibiotics only for high-risk hernia repairs
audits.setting: General surgical department (South Tyneside and Sunderland, Royal Marsden, Northumbria and North Tees affiliations)

cycle1.result: Perioperative antibiotics given in 87.8% overall: 89% elective groin, 85% elective ventral/umbilical, 80% emergency repairs.

audits.intervention: Departmental standardised 'high-risk criteria' defining when antibiotics are indicated, with departmental education.
audits.other_findings: Postoperative complication rates stayed low and did not increase.
audits.citation: Bleasdale E, Jones-Whiting L, Khaw R, Russ J, Cross J. 727 Implementing High-Risk Criteria to Optimise Perioperative Antibiotic Use in Hernia Surgery: A Two-Cycle Audit. British Journal of Surgery. 2026;113(Supplement_6). doi:10.1093/bjs/znag063.145.

audits.title: EP 179 Closed Loop Audit of Prophylactic Antibiotic Practices in Ventral Hernia Repair According to the Local Hospital Guidelines
audits.standard: Local guideline (in line with European and British Hernia Societies): prophylaxis only for high-risk mesh repair using the standard regimen

cycle1.result: Overall compliance 27.1%; unnecessary antibiotics in 35.6%; only 1 of 23 high-risk mesh patients received recommended prophylaxis.

audits.intervention: Departmental presentation of findings and educational posters.

cycle2.result: Overall adherence 80%; 90.9% compliance among high-risk mesh patients; 2 of 4 low-risk patients received unnecessary prophylaxis.

audits.citation: Elseed A, Romman S, Jama A. EP 179 Closed Loop Audit of Prophylactic Antibiotic Practices in Ventral Hernia Repair According to the Local Hospital Guidelines. British Journal of Surgery. 2026;113(Supplement_8). doi:10.1093/bjs/znag087.550.

audits.title: EP 184 Prophylactic Antibiotics in Groin Hernia Repair: Are We Compliant with Current Guidelines? Closed Loop Audit
audits.standard: HerniaSurge, European and British Hernia Society and trust guidelines: no routine prophylaxis for low-risk elective open mesh or laparoscopic repair

cycle1.result: 6 of 22 high-risk patients received compliant prophylaxis; antibiotics unnecessary in 32.5%; overall compliance 27.1%.

audits.intervention: Departmental presentation of findings and educational posters

cycle2.result: 90.9% of 11 high-risk patients compliant; 1 of 2 low-risk patients given unnecessary antibiotics; overall adherence 84.6%.

audits.other_findings: Baseline showed both overuse and inappropriate antibiotic selection.
audits.citation: Elseed A, Romman S. EP 184 Prophylactic Antibiotics in Groin Hernia Repair: Are We Compliant with Current Guidelines? Closed Loop Audit. British Journal of Surgery. 2026;113(Supplement_8). doi:10.1093/bjs/znag087.554.
